questions.template: Which of these is a job your skeleton does?
questions.hint: Think of your skull and ribs as armour!
questions.explain: Skeletons do three jobs: SUPPORT your body, PROTECT soft parts, and help you MOVE.

questions.hint: It's the helmet you were born wearing!
questions.explain: The skull is a bony helmet around the brain. Ribs guard the heart and lungs instead.

questions.template: Your ribs make a cage. What do they protect?
questions.hint: What's beating and breathing inside your chest?
questions.explain: The rib cage wraps around the heart and lungs like a fence of bone.

questions.template: Muscles move bones by working in…?
questions.hint: One pulls, its partner relaxes — then they swap!
questions.explain: Muscles can only PULL, never push — so they work in pairs, taking turns, like your biceps and triceps.

questions.template: Animals WITHOUT a backbone are called…?
questions.explain: Vertebrates (like Max!) have backbones; invertebrates like snails and insects don't — some wear skeletons OUTSIDE.

questions.template: Where two bones meet and let you bend is called a…?
questions.hint: Knees and elbows are famous ones!
questions.explain: Joints are the bendy meeting points of bones — knees, elbows, ankles and more.

questions.template: A crab's hard shell is a skeleton on the OUTSIDE. What's it called?
questions.explain: Exoskeletons are armour-skeletons on the outside. Ours are endoskeletons — 'endo' means inside.

questions.template: Which mineral makes bones strong — found in milk and leafy greens?
questions.hint: Nonna always said: strong bones drink their milk!
questions.explain: Calcium builds strong bones and teeth. Animals (and gladiators) get it from food — a balanced diet feeds the skeleton.
